Let $p>0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$. If any component of $\alpha$ is odd, then $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=0.$$ If $\alpha_j=2k_j$ for $j=1,2,3$, then $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=\pi^{3/2}\prod_{j=1}^3\frac{(2k_j)!}{4^{k_j}k_j!\,p^{k_j+1/2}}.$$ For every $q\in\mathbb N_0$, differentiation with respect to $p$ is valid and $$\frac{d^q}{dp^q}\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=(-1)^q\int_{\mathbb R^3}\|x\|_2^{2q}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx.$$

It may instead return `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; no success for every finite input or cap is asserted.

A **certified enclosure** for a real value is a nonempty closed interval $B=[a,b]$ with finite dyadic endpoints; for a complex value it is a nonempty closed rectangle $B=[a_1,b_1]+i[a_2,b_2]$ with finite dyadic endpoints. Its radius is half its length in the real case and half its Euclidean diagonal in the complex case; $d(B,0)$ is the Euclidean distance from $B$ to $0$. An evaluator item declares whether its input is an exact dyadic point or a dyadic interval/rectangle enclosure; a successful range result contains the exact function image of every admissible point in an input enclosure. Constants not exactly dyadic must be supplied with certified enclosing intervals or rectangles.

For real intervals, complex rectangles or complex balls on which an operation is defined, enlarging either input enclosure cannot shrink the computed enclosure: for binary $\circ\in\{+,-,\times,\div\}$, if $X\subseteq X'$ and $Y\subseteq Y'$, then the computed set enclosure of $X\circ Y$ is contained in that of $X'\circ Y'$ whenever both are finite results and their domain restrictions are preserved. The square-root enclosure is inclusion-isotone on nonnegative intervals. Each finite ball operation in [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] contains the exact ball image. A `split-domain`, `entire`, `domain-error`, `overflow`, or `inconclusive` status makes no finite claim. For a finite expression DAG whose operation nodes all return finite enclosures, every exact node value from every admissible input assignment belongs to its computed node enclosure; in particular, the root enclosure contains the exact range. If any node returns a non-finite status, no finite DAG enclosure is asserted.

Every finite interval returned for a requested real output node by [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] on an input interval in the domain of $\exp$, $\ln$, $\sqrt{\phantom{x}}$, $\arctan$, $\sin$, $\cos$, or $\tan$ contains the exact range of the corresponding function on that interval. For the same typed DAG and designated real output node, if all input intervals are nested coordinatewise, all constant enclosures are fixed, and both calls use the same finite dyadic format and truncation index $N$, then, whenever both calls return finite enclosures, the canonical branch-cell and fixed-term construction makes the smaller domain's computed enclosure a subset of the larger one's. An unresolved fixed branch, pole, invalid domain or overflow returns its stated non-finite status and carries no finite success claim.

The power-series sine and cosine satisfy the addition identities and $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$. For $A(t)=\arctan t$ from [[def-real-elementary-functions-and-domains]], $$ \sin(A(t))=t\cos(A(t)),\qquad \cos(A(t))>0, $$ so $A(t)$ is the inverse tangent with values in $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$ when $\pi=4A(1)$. It is odd; for $u,v\ge0$ with $uv<1$, $A(u)+A(v)=A((u+v)/(1-uv))$; and for $t>0$, $A(t)=\pi/2-A(1/t)$. In particular $\sin(\pi/2)=1$ and $\cos(\pi/2)=0$. Also, $$ \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239). $$ For every real $x$ there is an integer $k$ and $r=x-k\pi/2$ with $|r|\le\pi/4$; the sine and cosine of $x$ are obtained from those of $r$ by the quarter-period identities. For every real $r$ with $|r|\le1$ and every $N\ge0$, truncating sine through degree $2N+1$ and cosine through degree $2N$ gives absolute tail bounds $$ T_s=\frac{|r|^{2N+3}}{(2N+3)!(1-|r|^2/((2N+4)(2N+5)))} $$ and $$ T_c=\frac{|r|^{2N+2}}{(2N+2)!(1-|r|^2/((2N+3)(2N+4)))}. $$

For pair densities $f,g$ arising as finite products of Gaussian contractions in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], let $$\mathcal C(f,g)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\overline{f(x)}g(y)}{\|x-y\|_2}\,dy\,dx.$$ Then $\mathcal C$ is a well-defined Hermitian positive-semidefinite sesquilinear form on their finite linear span, and $$|\mathcal C(f,g)|^2\le\mathcal C(f,f)\mathcal C(g,g).$$ For orbitals $\phi_a,\phi_b,\phi_c,\phi_d$ and pair densities $f_{ab}=\overline{\phi_a}\phi_b$, the integral convention in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]] gives $$|G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_c,\phi_d)|\le\sqrt{G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_a,\phi_b)G(\phi_c,\phi_d;\phi_c,\phi_d)},$$ where each diagonal quantity is nonnegative. For the real finite energy functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]], let $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$, and define the primitive-space density coefficients $W_{ab}=\sum_{p,q=1}^r C_{ap}D_{pq}C_{bq}$. Reindexing the finite two-body energy gives $E_2=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b,c,d}W_{ab}W_{cd}G_{ab,cd}$. Thus for any finite set $S$ of primitive quartets omitted from that contraction, $$B_S=\frac12\sum_{(a,b,c,d)\in S}|W_{ab}W_{cd}|\sqrt{G_{ab,ab}G_{cd,cd}}$$ is an accumulated upper bound for the absolute omitted energy contribution. This does not assert that a screened integral is zero.

Let $n,r\ge1$, $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$ with $\|C\|_F\le B$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ with $\|D\|_F\le M$. Suppose $|\widetilde H_{ab}-H_{ab}|\le\varepsilon_2$ and $|\widetilde G_{abcd}-G_{abcd}|\le\varepsilon_4$ for every entry. With the functional of [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]], $$|\widetilde E-E|\le MrnB^2\varepsilon_2+\frac12M^2r^2n^2B^4\varepsilon_4,$$ and $$\|\nabla_C\widetilde E-\nabla_CE\|_F\le2nrBM\varepsilon_2+2n^2r^2B^3M^2\varepsilon_4.$$

citations.quote: Let $n,r\ge1$ be integers, $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$, $H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n\times n\times n}$. Define their transformed tensors by $$H'_{pq}=\sum_{a,b=1}^n C_{ap}H_{ab}C_{bq},\qquad G'_{pqrs}=\sum_{a,b,c,d=1}^n C_{ap}C_{bq}C_{cr}C_{ds}G_{abcd},$$ for $1\le p,q,r,s\le r$. Define the finite **variational energy functional** $$E(C;D,H,G)=\sum_{p,q=1}^r D_{pq}H'_{pq}+\frac12\sum_{p,q,r,s=1}^r D_{pq}D_{rs}G'_{pqrs}.$$ Its gradient $\nabla_C E$ is the ordinary Euclidean gradient with respect to the $nr$ real entries of $C$. The basis dimension is $n$, the contracted dimension is $r$, and for any finite matrix or tensor $A$, $\|A\|_F=(\sum |A_{i_1\ldots i_k}|^2)^{1/2}$, with the sum over all its entries. This is a finite algebraic functional; it assumes no Hartree–Fock, self-consistency, or minimizing-state postulate.

Let $n,r\ge1$, $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$ with $\|C\|_F\le B$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ with $\|D\|_F\le M$. Suppose $|\widetilde H_{ab}-H_{ab}|\le\varepsilon_2$ and $|\widetilde G_{abcd}-G_{abcd}|\le\varepsilon_4$ for every entry. With the functional of [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]], $$|\widetilde E-E|\le MrnB^2\varepsilon_2+\frac12M^2r^2n^2B^4\varepsilon_4,$$ and $$\|\nabla_C\widetilde E-\nabla_CE\|_F\le2nrBM\varepsilon_2+2n^2r^2B^3M^2\varepsilon_4.$$

derivations.claim: There are $2^4=16$ primitive entries, each perturbed by $\varepsilon$, and each product of four coefficients is $K^4$. Thus $\Delta G'_{1111}=16K^4\varepsilon$ and $\Delta E=\tfrac12\Delta G'_{1111}=8K^4\varepsilon$. The perturbed energy is $\tfrac12\varepsilon(C_1+C_2)^4$, so each gradient component is $2\varepsilon(C_1+C_2)^3=16K^3\varepsilon$; its two-entry Frobenius norm is $16\sqrt2K^3\varepsilon$.

Here $B=\|C\|_F=\sqrt2K$ and $M=\|D\|_F=1$. Substitution into [F2] gives energy bound $\tfrac12(1)^2(1)^2(2)^2(\sqrt2K)^4\varepsilon=8K^4\varepsilon$ and gradient bound $2(2)^2(1)^2(\sqrt2K)^3(1)^2\varepsilon=16\sqrt2K^3\varepsilon$, equal to the errors in step 1.1.

citations.quote: Let $a,b>0$, $A,B\in\mathbb R^3$, $p=a+b$, $\mu=ab/p$, and $P=(aA+bB)/p$. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\exp(-a\|x-A\|_2^2)\exp(-b\|x-B\|_2^2)=\exp(-\mu\|A-B\|_2^2)\exp(-p\|x-P\|_2^2).$$ For any multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N_0^3$, the polynomial factor $(x-A)^\alpha(x-B)^\beta$ is a finite polynomial in $x-P$ of total degree at most $|\alpha|+|\beta|$. Moreover, $P=(a/p)A+(b/p)B$ lies on the closed segment from $A$ to $B$.

Let $p>0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$. If any component of $\alpha$ is odd, then $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=0.$$ If $\alpha_j=2k_j$ for $j=1,2,3$, then $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=\pi^{3/2}\prod_{j=1}^3\frac{(2k_j)!}{4^{k_j}k_j!\,p^{k_j+1/2}}.$$ For every $q\in\mathbb N_0$, differentiation with respect to $p$ is valid and $$\frac{d^q}{dp^q}\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=(-1)^q\int_{\mathbb R^3}\|x\|_2^{2q}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx.$$

derivations.claim: By [F1]–[F2], the unnormalized overlap is $(\pi/(a+b))^{3/2}$ and each norm squared is $(\pi/(2a))^{3/2}$ or $(\pi/(2b))^{3/2}$. Multiplying by the normalization constants gives $S(h_a,h_b)=(2\sqrt{ab}/(a+b))^{3/2}$.

The Gram matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&S\\S&1\end{pmatrix}$, whose characteristic polynomial is $(1-\lambda)^2-S^2$, so its eigenvalues are $1\pm S$. At $a=b$, $S=1$ and the lower eigenvalue is zero. For $a\ne b$, $2\sqrt{ab}<a+b$, hence $0<S<1$; continuity of the displayed formula gives $S\to1$ as $b\to a$, and therefore $(1+S)/(1-S)\to\infty$.

citations.quote: For pair densities $f,g$ arising as finite products of Gaussian contractions in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], let $$\mathcal C(f,g)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\overline{f(x)}g(y)}{\|x-y\|_2}\,dy\,dx.$$ Then $\mathcal C$ is a well-defined Hermitian positive-semidefinite sesquilinear form on their finite linear span, and $$|\mathcal C(f,g)|^2\le\mathcal C(f,f)\mathcal C(g,g).$$ For orbitals $\phi_a,\phi_b,\phi_c,\phi_d$ and pair densities $f_{ab}=\overline{\phi_a}\phi_b$, the integral convention in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]] gives $$|G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_c,\phi_d)|\le\sqrt{G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_a,\phi_b)G(\phi_c,\phi_d;\phi_c,\phi_d)},$$ where each diagonal quantity is nonnegative. For the real finite energy functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]], let $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$, and define the primitive-space density coefficients $W_{ab}=\sum_{p,q=1}^r C_{ap}D_{pq}C_{bq}$. Reindexing the finite two-body energy gives $E_2=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b,c,d}W_{ab}W_{cd}G_{ab,cd}$. Thus for any finite set $S$ of primitive quartets omitted from that contraction, $$B_S=\frac12\sum_{(a,b,c,d)\in S}|W_{ab}W_{cd}|\sqrt{G_{ab,ab}G_{cd,cd}}$$ is an accumulated upper bound for the absolute omitted energy contribution. This does not assert that a screened integral is zero.

Every invocation of [[alg-finite-gaussian-basis-integral-recurrence-evaluation]] terminates after finitely many operations bounded by its work and child-evaluator caps. If it returns `success`, each integral interval contains the exact integral range over the supplied parameter boxes. For the real energy/gradient branch, the returned energy interval and gradient-error bound contain the corresponding values of the finite functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]]. The reported discarded-energy bound is at least the sum of the absolute Cauchy–Schwarz bounds for all skipped terms. The evaluator may return `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; no universal success or exact-sparsity claim is made.

**Inputs.** A finite list of Cartesian Gaussian basis contractions from [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], represented by finite dyadic intervals for real centers and positive exponents and by finite dyadic intervals or complex rectangles for coefficients; a finite nuclear list; and finite positive work, precision, integral-tolerance, energy-tolerance, and optional screening-tolerance caps. An energy/gradient request additionally requires real-valued basis contractions, real $C,D$, and finite bounds $B\ge\|C\|_F$, $M_D\ge\|D\|_F$ from [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]].
